description: Which refused-write banner an account earns from its billing status and from the last cycle's own write refusal: none, Sync paused, or Vault is full. One rule, three copies, because each shell reads its own BillingStatus and renders its own banner enum. Sync paused wins over a full vault, and a quota of zero is 'unknown' rather than 'full' — the second of those is why the stand-in server's filled quota shows no banner on an account that has stored nothing (futo-notes#178/#179 recorded it as unprovable on a device for that reason).
note: PARTIAL (test-reduction lever C, 2026-09-24): the TS (hostedBanner.test.ts) and Swift (formerly in HostedSetupModelTests.swift, now deleted) copies were dropped as per-shell replays; Kotlin's HostedSetupModelTest.kt banner cases are now the one asserted suite for this rule, with Rust's hosted_scenarios owning the engine behind it. The TS production copy was extracted out of createHostedSyncSettings.svelte.ts into its own file (futo-notes#186) so the `__testSync` hosted hook could assert on the same rule the sync screen renders — a second TS copy would have made the tests prove something that does not ship. A change to the precedence, to the zero-quota reading, or to how the last cycle's `SyncSummary.writeRefusal` feeds in (futo-notes C4) must still land in all three production copies in one commit. tests/cross-platform-sync.mjs continues to drive the TS production copy against a real stand-in server.
